title: Suvendu Adhikari says 17 Bengal rail projects cleared, seeks early opening of Sector V metro link
dek: After meeting Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw in Delhi, the chief minister said the stalled Chingrighata stretch of the New Garia-Sector V line was complete.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Thursday that 17 railway projects in West Bengal had been approved, after meeting Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw at Rail Bhavan in New Delhi, and asked for an early inauguration of the completed New Garia-Sector V metro stretch, according to reports.

The stretch, part of Kolkata's Orange Line, had been held up for months at Chingrighata in eastern Kolkata, where construction of a short elevated stretch across a busy crossing had stalled. Mr Adhikari said construction was now complete and trial runs had been held. The state wants Prime Minister Narendra Modi to open it, with a date to be set by the Prime Minister's Office, according to reports. In October, Kolkata Metro officials said they expected commercial services by December.

Mr Adhikari also asked for train services to start by March next year on the Hili and Nandigram-Deshapran lines, which he said had been held up by land disputes that were now resolved, and said about Rs 4,000 crore had been allocated for a rail link to Gangasagar, home of the Kapil Muni ashram, with the survey and detailed project report to be speeded up. He did not list the 17 projects, and the railway ministry had not released details by Friday morning.

Earlier in the day Mr Adhikari met Union Home Minister Amit Shah for nearly an hour and said they discussed development, law and order and welfare in the state.
